summary: Describes how FTP reply codes are used in TENEX mail processing, with the aim of more reliable mail service.

eli5.summary: When mail is delivered by file transfer, the receiving machine answers with number codes. This note explains how to use them to make delivery more reliable.

questions: what do ftp error codes 450 to 454 mean
how does tenex handle failed mail delivery
permanent vs temporary mail failure in ftp
subtitle: How TENEX sites will use the existing FTP error codes so mail senders can tell permanent failures from temporary ones.

tldr.problem: The FTP error codes for failed file actions did not distinguish the many causes of a mail delivery failure, so a mailing process could not decide whether to give up or try again.
tldr.mechanism: TENEX FTP servers will send 450 for permanent failures caused by the addressed user, 451 for permanent failures caused by the message, and 453 for temporary failures. Mailing processes will treat 450 and 451 as permanent and 452, 453 and 454 as temporary.
tldr.outcome: Mail senders can keep retrying temporary failures for several days and stop at once on permanent ones. The RFC says new FTP error codes were still being designed.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 630's status as Unknown and shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC itself describes an interim practice while new FTP error codes were being designed.

sections.title: The Problem With Mail Error Codes
sections.content:
RFC 630 is a short note from BBN about FTP error replies. The author says a major hindrance to reliable mail service is the lack of well-defined error replies that let a mailing process decide how to handle a failure.

New FTP error codes were still in the design stage. As an interim step, the RFC defines how TENEX sites intend to use the current codes, and informs all sites of it.
sections.eli5: If a letter cannot be delivered, the post office should say whether to try again tomorrow or give up. This note is about making that answer clear.

sections.title: The Existing Code Definitions
sections.content:
Five codes covered failure to perform a file action, including mail: 450 File not found, 451 File access denied to you, 452 Data connection closed, 453 Insufficient storage, and 454 Cannot connect to your data socket. Codes 450, 451 and 453 apply to both the MAIL and MLFL commands, while 452 and 454 only matter for MLFL.

There are more causes of mail failure than these five. Server implementors therefore made arbitrary assignments of conditions to codes. The reply text might tell a human what went wrong, but the code did not tell a process. The minimum distinction TENEX mail senders need is between permanent and non-permanent failures, because for the latter the process will try repeatedly for several days.
sections.eli5: There were only five numbers for many kinds of trouble, so people guessed which number to use. A computer reading the number could not tell what really went wrong.

sections.title: New TENEX Usage
sections.content:
The TENEX FTP server keeps using 452 and 454 as specified for MLFL. For MAIL and MLFL it sends the other codes this way: 450 for permanent failures due to the user addressed (no such user, no mailbox, or a mailbox net users cannot write in), 451 for permanent failures due to the message itself (for example a line over the TELNET connection that is too long, MAIL only), and 453 for temporary failures (TELNET connection unexpectedly closed, mailbox busy, unexpected local errors).

On the sending side, TENEX mailing processes then treated all of 450 to 454 as permanent. They will be changed to read 452, 453 and 454 as temporary and keep 450 and 451 permanent. The changes were to be installed over the next couple of months.
sections.eli5: Now 450 means 'this person cannot get mail', 451 means 'this letter is broken', and 453 means 'busy, try later'. The sender stops or retries to match.

sections.title: Compatibility With Other Sites
sections.content:
The RFC argues that the change should not hurt mail exchanges between TENEX and non-TENEX sites, because it simply swaps one arbitrary set of interpretations for another. It gives two supporting points.

Reading 450 and 451 as permanent and 452 to 454 as temporary is consistent with their original meanings. And the new choice of codes is no further from the original meanings than the old one, while conveying more information.
sections.eli5: Other computers will not be confused, because the new way is no more of a guess than the old way, and it tells them more.
